Tuazon]] |blank1_name = Political party |blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|National Unity Party (Philippines)}}|border=darkgray}} [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|NUP]] |blank2_name = Congressional bloc |blank2_info = Majority }} '''Leyte's 3rd congressional district''' is one of the five [[congressional districts of the Philippines]] in the province of [[Leyte (province)|Leyte]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1916 and earlier in the [[Philippine Assembly]] from 1907 to 1916.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 28, 2020}} The district consists of the old provincial capital, [[Leyte, Leyte|Leyte]], and adjacent municipalities of [[Calubian]], [[San Isidro, Leyte|San Isidro]], [[Tabango]] and [[Villaba]]. It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Anna Veloso-Tuazon|Anna Victoria V. Tuazon]] of the [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|National Unity Party]] (NUP).{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 28, 2020}} Until 1931, it consisted of the north-central municipalities of [[Abuyog]], [[Barugo]], [[Burauen]], [[Capoocan]], [[Carigara]], [[Dagami]], [[Hinunangan]], [[Hinundayan]], [[Jaro, Leyte|Jaro]], [[La Paz, Leyte|La Paz]], and [[Pastrana, Leyte|Pastrana]]. Following the creation of the [[Leyte's 5th congressional district|fifth district]], it was redefined to consist of the southern municipalities of undivided Leyte that now form part of [[Southern Leyte]],{{cite PH act|chamber=Act|number=3788|url=http://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l5564 |title=An Act Reorganizing the Representative Districts of the Province of Leyte and Creating a Fifth District|date=December 2, 1930 |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate= May 6, 2020}} until they were transferred to the [[Southern Leyte's at-large congressional district|new province's at-large district]] in 1961, three years after its establishment. The district was subsequently redefined to consist of the sub-province of [[Biliran]] and the northern municipalities of [[Calubian]], [[Isabel, Leyte|Isabel]], [[Leyte, Leyte|Leyte]], [[Matag-ob]], [[Merida, Leyte|Merida]], [[Palompon]], [[San Isidro, Leyte|San Isidro]], [[Tabango]], and [[Villaba]], all previously from the [[Leyte's 1st congressional district|first district]], from 1961 until its second dissolution in 1972.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=2227|url=https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1959/ra_2227_1959.html |title=An Act Creating the Province of Southern Leyte|date=May 22, 1959 |publisher=The Lawphil Project - Arellano Law Foundation, Inc. |accessdate=6 May 2020}} Re-established in 1987, it included its current northern municipalities and the sub-province of Biliran, which was separated effective 1995 as its [[1992 Philippine provincial creation plebiscites|provincial status]] and [[Biliran's at-large congressional district|separate representation]] were ratified in 1992.{{cite web|title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm|publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=April 10, 2020}}{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=7160|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1991/10/10/republic-act-no-7160/ |title=An Act Providing for a Local Government Code of 1991 |date=October 10, 1991 |publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)|Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 13, 2021}} ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan=2 | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan=2 | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Legislature ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" | Constituent
